text:
maria_customer: hey team, after we pinned our account to rwd-embed-v2 yesterday, our faiss index started rejecting upserts. previously vectors were 1536 but new embeddings are 1024. nothing else changed on our side. any idea why this happened? we pinned because v2 was supposed to be stable for us :worried:

sara_support: hi @maria_customer — sorry for the disruption. can you paste the exact error you're seeing from the upsert call and the model id/version you pinned to? also, do you still have any previously stored vectors (1536) in the index?

maria_customer: here's the DB error we get when upserting new items:

```
error: Vector length mismatch: provided=1024 expected=1536
at repo.upsert (vector_store.js:142:12)
HTTP 400
```

Pinned model info from our console: model: `rwd-embed-v2`, pinned_version: `rwd-embed-v2-2026-11-12-variant-a`

sara_support: thanks. alex from ML might know — pinging @alex_ml :eyes:

alex_ml: looking. two quick hypotheses: 1) the pinned variant is a smaller/different architecture (1024-d) and the pin pointed to a variant with lower dim, or 2) the client SDK is accidentally hitting a different model (header mismatch or regional routing). can you share the request payload you send for embeddings (redact API key)?

maria_customer: sure, here's the payload we POST to /v1/embeddings (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-v2",
  "input": ["doc1 text", "doc2 text"],
  "batch_size": 64
}
```

jordan_eng: quick note — pinning at the account level can map to a specific variant id behind the scenes. the UI shows the friendly name `rwd-embed-v2` but the actual pinned variant id matters for vector shape. @sara_support can you check the customer's pin metadata?

sara_support: pulled the pin metadata for the account: pinned_to = `variant-a-1024` (internal id `rwd-v2-var-a-1`). customer thought they pinned the general family but it ended up pinned to a 1024-d variant. i'm escalating to eng for advice on safe rollback. :exclamation:

alex_ml: yep that explains it — variant-a is an experimental smaller-embedding variant we rolled for throughput tests. it produces 1024-d embeddings. for customers who require 1536, we usually recommend pinning to `rwd-embed-v2-1536` (variant-b). two immediate remediation options:
  1) Re-pin the account to a 1536-d variant (`rwd-embed-v2-1536`) via the Console or PATCH /v1/accounts/:id/pins — this will make future embeddings 1536 again. BUT be careful: newly generated 1536 vectors won't match existing 1024 vectors and you'll need to reindex or keep dual indexes.
  2) If you need a quick compatibility layer, you can pad 1024 vectors to 1536 by appending zeros at inference time (temporary) or re-ingest all vectors from historical source. padding preserves some search behavior but is approximate.

maria_customer: ugh. we definitely don't want to reindex 2M items. is padding safe? any docs on that?

jordan_eng: padding is a pragmatic stopgap. downside: it implicitly changes similarity geometry. If you're using cosine similarity, padding with zeros keeps direction for the 1024 subspace, but relative magnitudes change if client code normalizes differently. Another option: run a small roll-forward where reads use a hybrid query: try querying both indexes (1024 and 1536) and merge results. Not trivial though.

infra-bot: deploy event: model-variants-sync job ran at 1876543195 — mapped `rwd-embed-v2` -> variants [rwd-v2-var-a-1(1024), rwd-v2-var-b-1536]

sara_support: for transparency — how did the pin choose variant-a? the Console's "pin" flow allows selecting a specific variant, but if you clicked the shorthand family name we default to the lowest-latency variant for Dedicated customers. we should improve that language. i'll file a console copy bug.

alex_ml: steps to reproduce locally (what I ran):

1) curl to list model variants:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/rwd-embed-v2/variants
```
response shows JSON listing variant ids and dims (look for `embedding_dim`).

2) simulate client calls:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-v2","input":["x"]}'
```
check response vector length.
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.12,...],"embedding_dim":1024}]}
```

alex_ml: if you want a safety net, we can create a pin alias that explicitly maps to `rwd-embed-v2-1536` for your account and schedule the change during a maintenance window. that avoids console confusion.

maria_customer: schedule sounds good. timeline? we can do late sunday window. Also what caused the variant mapping to change now? we didn't touch anything.

sara_support: looking through audit logs — there was a one-click "optimize for throughput" button used by an admin on the account last week. that sets a recommended pin to the lower-dim variant for cost/throughput gains. we should add an explicit confirmation dialog. i've attached the audit line: `admin_id=78 action=set_pin recommended=throughput`

jordan_eng: follow-up engineering notes (for internal):
- investigate improving Console pin UX to show `embedding_dim` prominently.
- add an API warning when pin change causes vector_dim mismatch for accounts with existing vector stores (we can inspect known indexes via metadata).
- consider adding a migration helper endpoint: POST /v1/indexes/:id/migrate?strategy=pad|reencode to automate padding/reencode ops.

alex_ml: for the customer now, proposed action plan:
  1) We create an explicit pin to variant-b (1536) and schedule at 2027-04-18 02:00 UTC.
  2) We run a quick compatibility check: sample 100 queries against both variants and compute hit overlap. If overlap > 85% you may be okay with padding; else we recommend reindex.
  3) Provide a script to pad 1024->1536 (zero append) and a small re-ranking tool to re-score top-K hits with the 1536 model to catch regressions.

maria_customer: thanks. please go ahead with the schedule. also can you share the sample checker script?

sara_support: attaching small sample-checker snippet below (bash + python hybrid). paste into your support ticket for download.

```
# sample-checker.sh
SAMPLE_IDS=(...)
for id in "${SAMPLE_IDS[@]}"; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-v2-1536","input":["'"$id"'" ]}' > /tmp/embed1536.json
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-v2-var-a-1","input":["'"$id"'" ]}' > /tmp/embed1024.json
  # compare cosine similarity on top-k
done
```

python snippet computes overlap and reports.

infra-bot: note: creating explicit pin alias requested by support for account 6644 at 1876543255 — pending approval.

maria_customer: appreciated. one last question — will billing change if we move back to 1536?

sara_support: yes cost per embedding token may increase slightly since vector size affects storage and sometimes pricing. i'll include estimated delta in the ticket.

alex_ml: final note — for long-term, if you want stable dims regardless of perf experiments, request a hard-pin to the full variant id (not family). that prevents the platform from selecting a cheaper variant. we'll also scope a console change to make that clearer. :thumbsup:
